title: Klanken van het Nederlands
summary: Long vs short vowels, the hard g, and sch

blocks.title: The vowel length system
blocks.body: Dutch vowels come in **short** and **long** pairs — and the difference changes the word. *man* (man) vs *maan* (moon). *bos* (forest) vs *boos* (angry). The rule: a double letter, or a single vowel in an open syllable, is long.

blocks.explain: Double *aa* = long vowel. *maan* is moon; *man* is man.

blocks.title: The famous g
blocks.body: The Dutch *g* (and *ch*) is a scrape at the back of the throat — like gently clearing your throat. *goed*, *gracht*, *gezellig*. In the Randstad it's hard; in the south it's softer. We learn the hard one — it's what you'll hear in Amsterdam.
blocks.callout: g and ch are the same sound: *acht* (eight) rhymes with the end of *dag*.

blocks.title: sch — the double scrape
blocks.body: *sch* is s + the hard g, back to back: *school*, *schrijven* (to write), and the word the Dutch use to test foreigners: *Scheveningen*. Don't panic — s, then scrape.
blocks.callout: At the end of a word, -isch sounds like 'ies': *logisch* = LO-gies.
